name: gethookd
tagline: AI generator for social video hooks and opening lines, built to stop the scroll.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This category is a prompt with a login screen. The actual product is a set of hook formulas, a system prompt that keeps output punchy, and a place to keep the ones that worked, all of which an agent can assemble in an afternoon. What you cannot clone is whatever performance data sits behind the paid version, assuming there is any, and the taste baked into their prompts after thousands of runs. The honest test: paste your topic into a decent model with ten named hook patterns and see if the output is materially worse. For most creators it is not, it is just less pretty.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a topic and audience, fans it out across a library of named hook formulas, and returns twenty ranked openers you can save, rate and export.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Your own swipe file of hooks that actually performed, if you want the output tuned
whatYouLose: Their hand-tuned prompts, which are probably better than your first draft
Any private data on which hook shapes actually convert
A polished UI on your phone while you are filming
Trend awareness, if the paid tool pulls in what is currently working
Someone else maintaining it when the model behind it changes
moatNotes: The only durable edge in hook tools is measured outcomes at scale. Without that it is a wrapper competing on interface.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because opening a purpose-built box that spits out twenty options beats staring at a blank chat window, and because the paid prompt has been sanded down by people who do this all day. Creators buy momentum, not technology. If you already have opinions about what a good hook looks like, the subscription is mostly buying you a nicer button.
notes: Judge it on output quality alone, since the moat is prompt taste and nothing structural.
prompt:
Build a local hook generator web app in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js 15 with the app router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3. Run it with npm run dev on localhost. No Docker, no Prisma, no auth.

Data model in SQLite:
- formulas: id, name, description, template, example
- runs: id, topic, audience, platform, tone, created_at
- hooks: id, run_id, formula_id, text, rating (null, up or down), notes

Seed the formulas table with at least twelve named hook patterns, each with a short description and a template. Cover these shapes: contrarian claim, specific number, mistake confession, before and after, direct callout of an audience, curiosity gap, urgency, fast tutorial promise, myth bust, personal stakes, comparison, and pattern interrupt question. Write real, usable templates, not placeholders.

Main page: a form with topic, target audience, platform (TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube long form), and tone. On submit, call one LLM (read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env.local, model name in a single constant) with a system prompt that enforces: under twelve words where possible, no hashtags, no emoji, spoken language not written language, no throat clearing. Ask for two hooks per formula in strict JSON and validate the shape before inserting.

Results view: hooks grouped by formula, each with a thumbs up or thumbs down button and a notes field, both persisted immediately. A sidebar lists past runs so I can reopen them.

Also build a /saved page listing every up voted hook across all runs, filterable by formula and platform, with a button that exports them to CSV.

In scope: generation, rating, history, export.
Out of scope: user accounts, payments, scheduling, posting to any platform, video editing, trend scraping, analytics.

Put the API key in .env.local and commit a .env.example. Write a README with setup in five lines or fewer. Keep the whole thing under twelve files and make sure it runs on a clean checkout after npm install.
